name: Zócalo
desc: A plaza so huge your rent worries feel small. Flag ceremonies, Aztec drummers, centuries stacked under your sneakers — zero pesos.

name: Bosque de Chapultepec
desc: Twice the size of Central Park, infinitely cheaper. Nap by the lake, dodge squirrels, pretend the castle on the hill is yours.

name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
desc: The Aztec sun stone lives here and a ticket costs less than your delivery fees. Save it for a rainy someday afternoon.

name: Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul)
desc: The blue house that launched a billion tote bags. Book ahead, cry a little, leave inspired and pleasantly broke.

name: Teotihuacán
desc: Pyramids older than the Aztecs, an hour from the city. Entry costs less than a latte; the goosebumps are complimentary.

name: Xochimilco Trajineras
desc: Rent a rainbow boat, split it eight ways, drift past floating mariachis with snacks in reach. Chaotic, floral, unbeatable.

name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
desc: Orange dome, marble everything, Rivera murals upstairs. Loiter outside for free; the inside costs pocket change.

name: Torre Latinoamericana
desc: Ride up 44 floors and watch the megacity blink to the horizon in every direction. Cheaper than therapy, better lighting.

name: Mercado de Coyoacán
desc: Tostadas the size of your ambitions in Frida's old neighborhood. Come hungry, leave broke in the best possible way.

name: Templo Mayor
desc: Aztec ruins hiding beside the cathedral like the city forgot to mention them. Entry: pocket change. Perspective: enormous.
